subject: general
question: Suresh borrows Rs. 80000 at 24% per annum simple interest and Ramesh borrows Rs. 91000 at 20% per annum simple interest. In how many years will their amounts of debts be equal?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Initial Principal** = 91000 − 80000 = ₹11000

Suresh annual interest = 24% of 80000 = ₹19200

Ramesh annual interest = 20% of 91000 = ₹18200

Difference in **Annual Interest** = 19200 − 18200 = ₹1000

Time required to equalize amounts = Principal Difference ÷ Interest Difference = 11000 ÷ 1000 = 11 years

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

For Suresh: **Principal (P₁)** = ₹80000, **Rate (R₁)** = 24% p.a.

For Ramesh: **Principal (P₂)** = ₹91000, **Rate (R₂)** = 20% p.a.

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/499bb86562934ce4d099f40ec148ac595bffbfeb1e81d3e95d7e9adab52e1e23.png] 

Let the **Time** be **T** years.

⇒ Suresh Amount = 80000 + (80000 × 24 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Suresh Amount = 80000 + 19200T

⇒ Ramesh Amount = 91000 + (91000 × 20 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Ramesh Amount = 91000 + 18200T

According to the question, **Suresh Amount = Ramesh Amount**:

⇒ 80000 + 19200T = 91000 + 18200T

⇒ 19200T − 18200T = 91000 − 80000

⇒ 1000T = 11000

⇒ T = 11000 ÷ 1000

⇒ T = 11 years

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Calculation

The total amount (A) is the sum of the principal (P) and the interest earned (SI). A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Rate Comparison

When two amounts with different principals and rates equalize, the person with the lower initial principal must have a higher interest rate to bridge the gap.
